• Lane: the nuclear-fuel upstream branch of spine 7, Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply
  • Boundary: this page only covers whether fuel supply can support faster time-to-power for advanced nuclear
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local raw packet proves that the company has public HALEU milestone disclosures, a DOE contract framework, and continuing issuer reporting.
  • Forward path: AI/data-center demand matters only if advanced-reactor projects and fuel arrangements convert into verifiable deliveries and revenue.
  • Current conclusion: the local evidence proves strategic position, not realized AI-linked revenue closure.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Issuer / press release: HALEU production milestone material
  • Issuer / contract release: DOE contract and cascade-construction material
  • Issuer / annual reports: continuing corporate disclosure baseline
  • Conclusion: this is a Needs-source fuel benchmark; the local packet does not yet tie advanced-nuclear demand directly to realized revenue

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials emphasize HALEU capability, government cooperation, and its strategic position in the Western nuclear-fuel chain.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep LEU as spine-7 nuclear-fuel context / benchmark, but not enough to write it as a realized data-center power beneficiary.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Whether data-center-linked advanced-nuclear projects already convert into realized LEU commercial revenue
  • Whether named customers, off-take structures, or repeat fuel purchases already form a verifiable loop
  • How short the lag really is between AI-load growth and LEU financial realization

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local evidence still cannot move the HALEU strategic story into verifiable commercial realization, LEU remains Needs-source context
  • If stronger local issuer/filing evidence shows the data-center time-to-power link remains mostly long-dated narrative, it can leave high-priority maintenance

docs.title: LITE — Lumentum
docs.text: Role: spine 4 photonic components / laser source / optical subsystem platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Lumentum sells the lasers, modules, and photonic subsystems behind AI optical networking. Its value is not only one module cycle; it sits across components, systems, CPO light sources, and scale-across monitoring inside the optical layer.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: LITE primary-owns the photonic-components / optical-subsystems node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI, with core exposure to EMLs, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, pluggable modules, and higher-power light sources. It does not primary-own switch silicon or AI system assembly; scale-across monitoring and WSS exposure still belong to the optical layer rather than the compute platform itself.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data centers demand more 800G, 1.6T, future 3.2T, CPO, and more complex DCI / scale-across optical links, Lumentum can raise shipments and mix through components, modules, laser sources, and some monitoring/control products. Profit depends on cloud demand, product mix, manufacturing execution, and the speed of next-platform adoption.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The investor overview describes Lumentum as a provider of optical and photonic technologies for AI, cloud computing, and next-generation communications, with products that include lasers, modules, and optical subsystems.
  • FY2025 Q4 net revenue was USD 480.7M, and Cloud & Networking revenue was USD 424.1M, or 88.2% of total revenue; management specifically highlighted strong demand in EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies for data-center interconnect, and 800G modules.
  • Q3 FY2026 net revenue was USD 808.4M, up 90.1% YoY and 21.5% QoQ; non-GAAP gross margin was 47.9%, and non-GAAP operating margin was 32.2%.
  • In Q3 FY2026 product-type revenue, Components were USD 533.3M and Systems were USD 275.1M.
  • Named OFC 2026 products included a 1.6T DR4 OSFP prototype with four 400G differential EMLs, an 800 mW SHP laser for CPO / silicon-photonics architectures, a 16-channel DWDM UHP laser source, and scale-across C-OCM / iTLA / WSS / DGE products.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• In the FY2025 Q4 results, management said AI data-center and long-haul demand gives the company confidence to surpass USD 600M in quarterly revenue by 2026-06 or earlier.
  • Q4 FY2026 guidance was revenue USD 960M-1.01B, non-GAAP operating margin 35.0%-36.0%, and non-GAAP diluted EPS USD 2.85-3.05.
  • Management said CPO and OCS should further increase earnings power; on this page those remain issuer claims rather than realized results.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Because Lumentum spans both components and systems, AI optical traffic growth does not need to monetize through only one module generation; multiple device and monitoring layers can convert the same networking upgrade into revenue.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Current local sources do not prove that Q3 FY2026 growth and margin levels can be linearly extrapolated for the long term.
  • Current sources do not precisely separate how much revenue and profit came from AI versus broader cloud, telecom, or other end markets.
  • When CPO, OCS, and broader scale-across products become material financial pillars is still mainly management direction rather than current proof.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Cloud AI demand slows and hits the components / modules mix first, pulling down revenue and margins.
  • Next-generation laser-source, CPO, or scale-across products fail to convert into volume production.
  • The company keeps AI-relevant products but cannot sustain component leadership and systems-level mix expansion.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: LITE is a Core / Market-found optical / photonics platform name. Reported financials prove growth across Cloud & Networking and the Components / Systems businesses, but the current sources do not separately identify AI-specific revenue or profit; further lift from CPO / OCS still needs later financial confirmation.

docs.title: META — Meta Platforms
docs.text: Role: spine 1 owned-capacity demand benchmark; advertising/assistant provide demand feedback Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-29; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Meta earns mainly from Family of Apps advertising and reinvests that cash in recommendation systems, models, assistants, glasses, and owned data centers. AI already affects ad delivery and engagement, but Meta is not a merchant cloud: most infrastructure is monetized indirectly through its own products.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Meta is an owned-hyperscale capacity buyer in Cloud and Compute Demand. It creates real demand for GPU, network, power, facility, and storage supply, but recovers the investment mainly through ad prices, impressions, and retention—unlike cloud-usage revenue at MSFT/AMZN/GOOG.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Recommendation and ad models can improve engagement, impressions, conversion, and price per ad. Assistants, models, and glasses may create new entry points, but their business models remain less proven. Capex creates value only if incremental ad/product cash exceeds depreciation and operating cost.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 56.31B, up 33%; operating margin was 41%.
  • Family daily active people were 3.56B; ad impressions rose 19% and average price per ad rose 12%.
  • Quarterly capex including finance-lease principal was USD 19.84B; FCF was USD 12.39B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • FY2026 capex outlook increased to USD 125-145B, partly for data-center costs supporting future capacity; this is forward guidance rather than realized capex.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Advertising cash flow and first-party distribution can support long-duration model/assistant scale and improve ad effectiveness and retention.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Meta does not fully disclose standalone AI revenue or ROI. Not all ad growth is AI, and assistants, glasses, or superintelligence are not yet established high-profit revenue streams.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Meta is a major capacity buyer and demand read-through, not an infrastructure seller. Value capture remains mostly ad economics; demand scale without engagement, pricing, or new revenue does not ensure shareholder return.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Capex/depreciation outgrow advertising revenue, operating income, and FCF.
  • AI recommendation increases usage while ad pricing, conversion, or user quality weakens.
  • Reality Labs, assistants, or glasses fail to produce durable returns.
  • Privacy, safety, youth-protection, or antitrust rules constrain data and advertising.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: META is a Context / Market-found owned-capacity demand benchmark. It validates hyperscale capex but owns no supply-chain primary node.

docs.title: MRVL — Marvell Technology
docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI Action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Marvell's core business is supplying switching, interconnect, optical-connectivity, and custom accelerated-infrastructure silicon for data centers and network infrastructure. It is not a general compute-platform owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Its primary ownership is data-center networking / optical.
  • Its secondary ownership is custom silicon / XPU exposure.
  • This page treats switching, interconnect, and optical connectivity as the first-line lens.
  • This page does not treat Marvell as a GPU, CPU, or full-system owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: AI-cluster expansion first lifts demand for switching, interconnect, optical connectivity, and custom infrastructure silicon, then flows into Marvell's data-center revenue. Custom silicon is an incremental source, not the primary ownership on this page.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FY2026 revenue was USD 8.195B, up 42% year over year, and the results release attributed the growth to AI demand.
  • The company's data-center solutions page explicitly places Marvell in custom accelerated infrastructure silicon and data-center connectivity.
  • NVIDIA and Marvell announced an NVLink Fusion strategic partnership.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Partnership materials say the companies will collaborate on silicon photonics; that is future collaboration framing, not realized shipment or revenue.
  • Management said year-over-year growth should accelerate in each quarter of FY2027 and that bookings continue to grow.
  • NVLink Fusion materials say Marvell will provide custom XPUs and NVLink Fusion-compatible scale-up networking.
  • Partnership materials say NVIDIA invested USD 2B in Marvell, but that ecosystem language is not the same as disclosed long-term revenue share.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• MRVL's primary ownership in the AI chain belongs under networking / optical, not under a custom-silicon-only narrative.
  • Custom silicon clearly adds upside, but it remains secondary exposure and should not displace the core switching, interconnect, and optical role.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The page does not have issuer-primary line-item proof for how much revenue NVLink Fusion will generate for MRVL.
  • The page does not have enough raw evidence to allocate MRVL's share inside hyperscaler programs or the broader NVIDIA ecosystem.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer-primary material no longer supports data-center networking / optical as the primary role, this page's role should be rewritten.
  • If the AI-growth story narrows to a single custom-program narrative without broader interconnect evidence, MRVL's durable role should be downgraded.
  • If partnership language persists without additional product or revenue realization, the page should not raise the weight of secondary custom-silicon exposure.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: active / Market-found. Primary ownership is networking / optical, with custom silicon kept as secondary exposure only.

docs.text: Role: spine 1 demand / capacity economics; enterprise AI production is secondary Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-04-29; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Microsoft earns Azure consumption, Microsoft 365/Dynamics/security subscriptions, and enterprise software fees. AI raises its data-center demand while creating billable Copilot, Azure AI, and agent usage. The key test is whether that usage grows fast enough to cover infrastructure investment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: In Cloud and Compute Demand, Microsoft is a hyperscale capacity buyer and merchant-cloud operator. It also owns enterprise workflow distribution in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle. Unlike accelerator vendors or pure application benchmarks, Microsoft controls cloud infrastructure, developer tooling, and enterprise seats.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Training, inference, and agents on Azure generate consumption revenue. Copilot, security, data, and business applications can add seats, usage, or premium bundles. Contracts enter RPO and convert as services are delivered. Economics depend on utilization, model/chip cost, capacity timing, and software attach—not capex alone.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 revenue was USD 82.9B, up 18%; operating income was USD 38.4B, up 20%.
  • Microsoft Cloud revenue was USD 54.5B, up 29%; Azure and other cloud services grew 40%.
  • Commercial RPO reached USD 627B, up 99%.
  • The AI business surpassed a USD 37B annual revenue run rate, up 123%.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: The enterprise installed base and Azure distribution lower adoption friction and support cross-sell across cloud, security, data, and workflow products.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: RPO and Azure growth are not wholly AI. The disclosed AI run rate does not provide standalone margin, and durable Copilot/agent ARPU still needs usage and renewal proof.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Microsoft's advantage is dual infrastructure and workflow distribution, not permanent leadership by one model. It is already market-found; the issue is whether AI revenue, utilization, and operating leverage outpace capex and model cost.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Azure/AI growth slows while data-center depreciation and capex keep rising.
  • Copilot or agent usage fails to become renewal, ARPU, or measurable productivity value.
  • Model partnerships/dependencies worsen cost, governance, or differentiation.
  • Security incidents, antitrust action, or bundling limits weaken distribution.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MSFT is a Core / Market-found demand entity with a secondary AI-production link.

docs.title: MTSI — MACOM
docs.text: Role: spine 4 analog / driver copper-optical enabling components Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-03-17; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: MACOM is more of a lower-level component supplier inside AI networking than a headline platform winner. It sells the drivers, equalizers, and related semiconductor parts that help 1.6T / 3.2T optical transceivers and high-density copper interconnects work.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MTSI primary-owns the enabling-components node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI, especially optical modulator drivers and scale-up copper cable driver / equalizer products. It does not primary-own full pluggable modules, switch silicon, or AI systems; the most durable role here is a component supplier inside the interconnect layer.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: If AI networking keeps moving toward 400G per lane, 1.6T / 3.2T optical modules, and denser scale-up copper, MACOM can add shipments and content through drivers, equalizers, and related analog connectivity parts. Its upside comes more through component-level design wins than through owning the full platform share.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• MACOM describes itself as a semiconductor-products supplier and, on 2026-03-17, announced two new 448G PAM4 modulator drivers for next-generation 1.6T and 3.2T optical transceivers.
  • Those drivers are explicitly described as supporting 400G per lane transmission and working with silicon-photonics, EML, and TFLN modulators.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• A 2026-03-16 release positions a cable driver with equalizer for next-generation scale-up connectivity and low-power, high-density copper, and as an alternative to retimed architectures; these are product-positioning and performance claims.
  • The company says the 448G drivers can accelerate customer time-to-market for next-generation connectivity systems and support AI, ML, and HPC data-center architectures.
  • Management says the new copper cable-driver solution can increase data throughput while preserving copper’s cost and power advantages.
  • The linked MACOM PDF is only a local stub, so any broader corporate financial or product framing that may exist there is not treated as verified fact on this page.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: As long as AI interconnect upgrades continue to need both optical and copper paths, a component-layer supplier like MACOM can capture some content in each speed transition, even if it does not present the same narrative intensity as pure module or end-platform vendors.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Current local sources do not prove that AI data center has become a dominant part of MACOM’s financial profile.
  • Current sources do not prove stable leadership share in 1.6T / 3.2T optical drivers or scale-up copper.
  • This page also does not prove revenue attribution across the broader optical catalog; it only confirms the direction and positioning of the named products.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• 400G per lane optical-driver or scale-up copper products fail to convert into sustained design wins and production volume.
  • Interconnect roadmaps shift toward other component approaches or other suppliers, reducing MACOM’s content.
  • AI-relevant components remain present but too small inside the broader company to create a durable role upgrade.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MTSI is the Active / Market-found spine 4 enabling-components name. The component positioning is real, but current local evidence is still closer to product-level fit than to a fully financially amplified core thesis.

docs.title: MU — Micron Technology
docs.text: Role: spine 3 HBM / DRAM / NAND physical-memory anchor Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-03-18; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Micron earns from DRAM, HBM, and NAND shipments. AI training/inference raises memory bandwidth and capacity demand; HBM increases value per bit, but memory remains highly cyclical. Record revenue, margin, and FCF prove monetization while increasing cycle-reversal risk.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MU primary-owns the physical-memory/HBM node in Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement. Accelerator architecture belongs to Semiconductors and Foundational Compute, and manufacturing/package realization to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. Enterprise data/context platforms such as SNOW remain in spine 9, not physical storage.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Accelerator/server platforms use more HBM/DRAM/NAND bits and higher-value mix. Micron monetizes volume, ASP, share, and product mix. Pricing, yield, HBM share, capex, and supply discipline determine profit; shortage can amplify returns and trigger the next supply cycle.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• FQ2 FY2026 revenue was USD 23.860B, versus USD 13.643B in FQ1 and USD 8.053B a year earlier.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was 74.4%/74.9%; adjusted FCF was USD 6.899B.
  • Cloud Memory BU revenue was USD 7.749B; Core Data Center BU revenue was USD 5.687B.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: FQ3 guidance was revenue USD 33.5B ± 0.75B and gross margin near 81%; management calls memory strategic in the AI era. Pricing, shipments, and cash must validate the guide.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: HBM bandwidth and package complexity can make memory value per accelerator much higher than conventional server configurations.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Record pricing/margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. Cloud/Core Data Center is not wholly AI/HBM, and capex, competitor supply, or customer digestion can create a cycle peak.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• HBM share, yield, or qualification lags and premium mix weakens.
  • DRAM/NAND supply outruns demand, collapsing ASP and gross margin.
  • Customer inventory or accelerator delivery enters a digestion period.
  • Capex rises while FCF and ROIC deteriorate materially through the cycle.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MU is the Core / Market-found physical-memory anchor. HBM is proven rather than hidden; historical market-action overlays do not belong on this page.

docs.title: MXL MaxLinear
docs.text: Role: spine 4 optical DSP / signal-chain modifier Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Modifier: former-half-hidden Evidence through: 2026-07-07; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: MaxLinear earns from broadband connectivity chips and high-speed interconnect chips. Its AI relevance comes from Keystone 400G/800G DSPs, AEC adjacency, and the Rushmore/Washington path into 1.6T optical/copper interconnect, but AI revenue and customers are still not disclosed separately.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: MXL primary-owns the optical DSP / high-speed signal-chain node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a module OEM, switch vendor, or cloud operator; external manufacturing and packaging execution still belong in Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Module vendors, cable vendors, and data-center interconnect customers buy Keystone, Washington, and related parts, creating optical DSP, TIA, and AEC revenue. If hyperscale scale-up / scale-out programs keep entering production ramps, infrastructure revenue should show up first in company results. Real AI monetization still depends on product revenue splits, customer proof, and profit improvement, not the roadmap alone.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 revenue was USD 137.188M, up about 43%.
  • Management said infrastructure revenue grew >130%, and the later source refresh restated that as +136%.
  • The company tied growth to production ramps of optical data-center products at multiple hyperscale customers.
  • Keystone is defined as a 400G/800G PAM4 DSP; OFC 2026 materials said it has been adopted by module vendors and hyperscale data-center customers, with millions of units shipped.
  • Rushmore was launched as a 1.6T PAM4 DSP family for AI/ML and data-center networks, and Washington was launched as a 200G/lane TIA for 1.6T optical transceiver modules.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Q2 FY2026 revenue guide was USD 160M-170M, midpoint USD 165M.
  • Management described Q1 as the start of a multi-year growth phase driven by optical data-center connectivity.
  • The company frames Keystone volume production, Rushmore sampling, Washington availability, and Makalu 3.2T retimer sampling as the next-stage narrative.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If Keystone adoption keeps converting into revenue and profit, MXL fits better as a small-base optical DSP / signal-chain modifier than as a legacy broadband/connectivity cycle name.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named hyperscaler revenue is not proven.
  • Keystone revenue dollars, customer count, and backlog are not proven.
  • Rushmore / Washington material revenue is not proven.
  • Silicon Motion dispute risk is not proven to be substantially resolved.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Silicon Motion arbitration turns materially adverse and absorbs the operating repair.
  • Infrastructure growth stalls and Keystone / Washington / Rushmore fail to convert into revenue or profit improvement.
  • The company cannot produce any durable AI / data-center revenue bridge and customer concentration stays high.
  • Competitors displace MaxLinear in optical DSP, AEC, or 1.6T signal-chain adoption.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: MXL is an Active / Market-found interconnect modifier. The old “half-hidden” label is no longer accurate, but this page still does not equate product presence with proven AI revenue quality.

docs.title: NET — Cloudflare
docs.text: Role: spine 9 edge / security / developer / AI delivery platform Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Unified ledger: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Cloudflare makes money from edge network, security, Zero Trust, developer-platform, and application-delivery subscriptions and usage. Its spine-9 role is enabling lower-latency deployment, delivery, and protection for APIs, applications, agents, and AI inference traffic, not owning hyperscaler capacity, E6 systems integration, or physical infrastructure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NET primary-owns the edge / security / developer delivery surface in AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle, while remaining adjacent to developer distribution in Platform Technology, Internet, and Distribution. It is not an application/data owner, does not primary-own E2 silicon or E6 systems, and does not own E7/E8 physical infrastructure. The failure point it controls is edge delivery, API protection, and network security for AI apps and agent runtime.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Revenue appears only when customers place AI apps, agents, APIs, and inference traffic on the edge runtime or network-security layer, driving Workers, delivery, security, and Zero Trust services. AI becomes revenue through usage, attach, and developer adoption. Broad network traffic, broad revenue, or total RPO do not automatically equal AI delivery revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue was USD 639.8M, up 34% year over year.
  • Current RPO growth was 34%.
  • Non-GAAP operating income was USD 73.1M; GAAP operating loss was USD 62.0M.
  • The local 2026-06-28 SEC latest-route packet shows that subsequent locally visible filings were mainly DEFA14A, Form 4, and 144 routes, with no newer operating print added to this page's source set.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Management describes AI as a fundamental re-platforming of the Internet and one of the company's major tailwinds.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI apps require lower-latency delivery, more API protection, more developer runtime, and tighter bot/agent security, Cloudflare's edge platform can expand attach and usage.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The company does not separately disclose AI revenue. Broad revenue, RPO, or edge traffic are not automatically AI delivery monetization.
  • "AI is re-platforming the Internet" still needs more specific Workers / AI / security adoption and economics proof before it can be treated as a separate AI revenue line.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: NET captures value through edge delivery, developer surface, and security attach, not by becoming an alternative hyperscaler, server owner, or facility-infrastructure beneficiary. The easiest misread is to write all AI network traffic as Cloudflare revenue, or to blur the developer edge platform into application/data ownership.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI-related usage stays mostly narrative, without clearer attach, retention, or revenue proof.
  • Hyperscaler, CDN, SASE, and developer-platform competition compress pricing or attach rates.
  • Developer/runtime adoption expands while GAAP losses and unit economics do not improve.
  • Edge/security demand grows without translating into a higher-quality recurring-revenue mix.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NET is a Core / Market-found spine-9 edge / security / developer / AI delivery platform.

docs.title: NOK — Nokia Oyj
docs.text: Role: spine 4 IP / optical connectivity context Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Needs-source Evidence through: 2026-06-05; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Nokia earns from platform-scale network businesses across Network Infrastructure, Mobile Networks, and Cloud and Network Services. Its AI relevance mainly comes through optical, IP, data-center networking, and the Infinera addition, but this page remains context because the company-level AI / cloud story is not yet split into stable enough product-level revenue proof.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Nokia primary-owns the IP / optical connectivity large-platform node in AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI. It is not a pure switch vendor, pure optical-module vendor, or single data-center silicon name; mobile, fixed, and broader telecom mix still dilute the primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: When AI / cloud customers buy optical line systems, pluggables, IP routing, data-center switching, and intra-data-center optics, the revenue should first appear inside Network Infrastructure, Optical Networks, and IP Networks. To write this as a stronger thesis, the page still needs more stable product-level or customer-level revenue bridges.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• In Q1 FY2026, AI & Cloud customer net sales grew 49% and were 8% of group sales.
  • Nokia booked EUR 1B of AI & Cloud customer orders in the quarter.
  • In the same quarter, Network Infrastructure net sales grew 6%, including 20% growth in Optical Networks.
  • The official data-center networking page explicitly places high-performance switches, optics, and IP / optical interconnect inside data centers and to / from / between data centers, including 800GE and intra-data-center optics.
  • Nokia says the Infinera deal expands webscale exposure; official materials state that webscale / ICP customers were over 30% of Infinera sales and that Infinera had been developing high-speed, low-power intra-data-center optical components suited to AI workloads.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management raised the 2026 Network Infrastructure growth assumption to 12%-14% and the Optical + IP Networks growth assumption to 18%-20%.
  • Nokia raised its 2025-2028 AI & Cloud addressable-market CAGR assumption to 27%.
  • New DSP / optical solution timing from OFC remains product and volume-roadmap language that still needs follow-through.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Nokia has real AI / cloud optical and IP exposure, but it still looks more like one growth pocket inside a large platform than a standalone pure AI interconnect asset.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• A durable revenue split from AI / cloud into optical, IP, switching, or Infinera content is not proven.
  • It is not proven that AI / cloud orders are already converting into a structurally better profit mix.
  • It is not proven that the AI optical / IP story can outweigh legacy mobile / fixed / telecom cycle noise.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• AI & Cloud orders fail to keep converting into revenue or margin.
  • Optical / IP growth gets offset by weakness in other large segments.
  • Infinera integration, R&D burden, or execution complexity erodes returns.
  • Data-center networking products fail to win durable share and the AI exposure falls back to concept-level relevance.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NOK is a Context / Needs-source large-platform IP / optical connectivity reference name. It helps explain the mainline, but current proof is still too broad to support a stronger pure AI interconnect conclusion.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: ServiceNow turns deployed compute into enterprise workflow and system-of-action platform revenue. The real test is not the model itself but whether AI moves from answering questions into governed workflow execution and then into durable ACV, subscription, and RPO growth.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: E9 AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle workflow / platform AI owner, centered on ITSM, CSM, HR, and enterprise-operations governed execution.
  • Boundary: it owns workflow, approval, ticket, and orchestration layers. It does not own E2 compute silicon, E6 systems manufacturing/integration, or any E7/E8 power and facility layer.
  • Distinction: NOW owns the workflow-execution control point. It is not CRM's customer-data control plane and not hyperscale cloud infrastructure.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• The core platform subscription base still carries the main seat and workflow revenue.
  • Now Assist, Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, and Build Agent Skills can expand contract value if they increase attach and net-new ACV.
  • cRPO and RPO show future contract conversion, but broad subscription growth, cRPO, and total revenue are not direct AI revenue.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2026 subscription revenue was USD 3.671B, up 22%.
  • Q1 FY2026 total revenue was USD 3.770B, up 22%.
  • cRPO was USD 12.64B, up 22.5%.
  • Total RPO was USD 27.7B, up 25%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The count of Now Assist customers spending more than USD 1M in annual contract value grew more than 130% year over year.
  • There were 16 net-new ACV transactions above USD 5M, nearly +80% year over year.
  • Context Engine, Autonomous Workforce, Build Agent Skills, and EmployeeWorks were all named directly in the Q1 issuer packet.
  • FY2026 subscription-revenue guidance includes about 125 bps of Armis contribution and management-expected operating-margin and FCF-margin headwinds. This is forward comparability framing, not a realized result.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• NOW sits at the workflow-execution and governance node, so it has one of the cleanest paths to turn enterprise AI from assistant behavior into governed action.
  • If more cross-system workflows consolidate on NOW, AI can expand platform spend rather than just add a feature to existing seats.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• There is still no CRM-like direct AI ARR disclosure for NOW.
  • Broad subscription revenue, cRPO, and RPO are not directly attributable AI revenue.
  • Current disclosure does not fully separate organic workflow/AI growth from the Armis contribution.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If Now Assist and Autonomous Workforce improve product narrative but fail to expand net-new ACV, NOW should fall back to a feature-strength story.
  • If workflow AI stays in pilot mode rather than governed production execution, the E9 owner case weakens.
  • If Armis contribution or integration headwinds keep obscuring organic net-new ACV and cash quality, NOW's benchmark quality should be downgraded.

docs.title: NVDA — NVIDIA
docs.text: Role: spine 2 accelerator platform / system architecture Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-20; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: NVIDIA earns from GPUs/accelerators, networking, systems, and enterprise software licenses/subscriptions. Its moat is the combined CUDA, interconnect, system design, and release cadence—not one GPU. AI workloads first become compute/networking shipments; mix, pricing, and software attach determine profit and cash.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVDA primary-owns the accelerator platform in Semiconductors and Foundational Compute. HBM belongs to Memory, Storage, and In-System Data Movement, wafer/package realization to Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials, and rack manufacturing to Systems, Racks, and Complex Manufacturing. These dependencies do not belong inside NVIDIA's primary lane.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Cloud, enterprise, and sovereign customers buy GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch, networking, and systems. Platform value comes from system ASP, software/services, iteration speed, and switching cost. Returns still depend on supply, gross margin, cash conversion, and installed-base utilization.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 FY2027 revenue was USD 81.6B, up 85%; Data Center revenue was USD 75.2B, up 92%.
  • Data Center compute revenue was USD 60.4B, up 77%; networking revenue was USD 14.8B, up 199%.
  • GAAP/non-GAAP gross margin was about 74.9%/75.0%, showing strong current value capture.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: NVIDIA attributes future growth to agentic/physical AI, AI factories, and expansion beyond hyperscale. This forward claim needs later revenue-mix proof.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Software, interconnect, and systems integration raise switching costs and let NVIDIA capture more than single-chip value.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: Current growth and margin cannot be perpetually extrapolated. Not all hyperscaler capex becomes NVIDIA revenue, and custom silicon, export controls, or supply shifts can change share and pricing.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Data Center growth, gross margin, or networking attach slows materially for several periods.
  • Large customers increase custom silicon and weaken accelerator share or bargaining power.
  • Export limits, advanced packaging/HBM supply, or system delivery blocks recognized revenue.
  • Competing platforms close the software/system total-cost gap.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NVDA is the Core / Market-found compute-platform anchor. The market already recognizes its AI role.

docs.title: NVT — nVent
docs.text: Role: Phase 5 E8 spine 8 site electrical boundary to energized rack; NVT is the enclosures / connectivity / liquid-cooling / power-distribution benchmark Structural status: context Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-05-01; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: nVent sits closer than ETN to the rack-adjacent mix of enclosures, power connections, control buildings, and cooling. It is not a generation owner or a server owner. In E8 it is the benchmark for rack-entry electrical / cooling exposure.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: NVT covers the inside-the-fence electrical and room-entry layer: cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, bus systems, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions. It does not own upstream generation / fuel, and it does not own E6 servers / network systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As AI data-center density rises, rack-adjacent demand also rises for enclosures, power connections, busway, control buildings, PDU support, liquid-cooling support, and mission-critical protection. NVT monetizes AI by helping deliver power and thermal management safely to the rack rather than by selling compute.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The annual report and Q1 2026 10-Q state that nVent's portfolio includes cable management, control buildings, liquid / air cooling, electrical connections, enclosures, equipment protection, power connections, and power management solutions.
  • Systems Protection is defined as serving mission-critical applications including data centers and includes custom enclosures, liquid / air cooling, control buildings, switchgear systems, and power distribution solutions.
  • The Electrical Products Group acquisition is described as infrastructure solutions primarily for power utilities and data centers, operated mainly within Systems Protection.
  • The SC25 issuer product capture shows nVent actively selling a liquid-cooling and power portfolio into data-center and networking infrastructure.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• nVent describes itself as an enclosures and liquid-cooling leader and explicitly targets data-center / networking infrastructure as an application lane.
  • Company-wide backlog increased from USD 749.3M at year-end 2024 to USD 2.3499B at year-end 2025; management attributed the increase mainly to the Electrical Products Group acquisition and growth in the data-centers business and expected most backlog to ship in 2026. That company-wide total is not AI-backlog proof.
  • Q1 2026 disclosed USD 75.8M of acquired customer backlog with an estimated useful life of about three years, showing management tracks acquired backlog conversion, but that still does not equal fully closed organic AI monetization.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• Within E8, NVT is a more focused benchmark than ETN for rack-entry electrical / cooling because it directly covers the enclosure, connection, power-distribution, and liquid-cooling stack.
  • Backlog growth still reflects both acquisition and data-center growth, so the stronger evidence should not be translated mechanically into all-organic AI upside.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current raw packet still does not provide clean hyperscaler / data-center revenue share, organic backlog-growth split, or standalone margin disclosure for liquid cooling / power distribution.
  • former-half-hidden remains only a workflow modifier and should not be treated as a formal state or as a hidden-thesis conclusion.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If backlog growth remains mostly acquisition-driven without clearer organic data-center conversion, NVT's AI beneficiary profile is being overstated.
  • If the enclosure / connectivity / liquid-cooling offering does not translate into clearer customer, revenue, or margin proof, the benchmark role should remain context-only.
  • If data-center spend cools and NVT cannot prove durable attach rates for rack-entry electrical / cooling, the current positioning should not be upgraded.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: NVT is the Context / Market-found enclosures / connectivity / liquid-cooling / power-distribution benchmark in E8. former-half-hidden remains only a workflow modifier, not a formal discovery state.

docs.title: NVTS — Navitas
docs.text: Updated: 2026-07-13 Industry page: AI Interconnect, Optical Networking, and DCI State: context / Needs-source

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Navitas belongs here as E8 high-voltage power semiconductor context: the local packet proves it has GaN/SiC products and high-voltage reference paths relevant to AI facility and rack power, but it does not support treating Navitas as an owner of E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems, and it does not close AI revenue into a durable investment judgment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Navitas sits at the high-voltage power-semiconductor layer on the facility / rack-power side of the stack. The local evidence supports roles in GaN/SiC, 400V DC data-center power, and 800V-to-50V / 800V-to-6V reference paths; it does not support claiming ownership of generation assets, GPU/ASIC compute silicon, or complete systems.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: The revenue chain only closes if AI facilities or racks adopt higher-voltage DC architectures, Navitas parts or reference paths are actually designed into the PSU, PDB, or DC-DC stages, and those design-ins convert into recurring production shipments. The current local sources mostly prove product capability, reference paths, and ecosystem positioning, not direct AI revenue capture.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text: Company product material, SEC filings, and local raw captures prove that Navitas has high-power GaN/SiC products and has published 400V DC AI data-center material, a 10kW 800V DC-DC platform, and related 800V-to-50V / 800V-to-6V reference demonstrations.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Issuer-led material places those platforms inside the AI data-center and rack-power upgrade story, including 800 VDC / MGX ecosystem showcase language; that is issuer or ecosystem positioning, not proof of a purchase agreement, production order, or closed revenue attribution.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: If AI facilities and racks keep moving toward 400V/800V HVDC and Navitas parts make it into production BOMs, it can benefit as an E8 high-voltage power-semiconductor supplier. That remains facility / rack-power context, not ownership of the broader AI power stack.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: The local packet does not yet close named hyperscaler or OEM production volume, AI revenue mix, durable BOM share, or sustained AI-driven margin improvement.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text: If later local evidence shows that AI rack-power upgrades are standardizing around branches that do not use Navitas parts, this page should be removed from active context or downgraded further. As long as issuer positioning has not turned into verifiable design-in and production-shipment evidence, the name must remain Needs-source.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Context / Needs-source. E8 role: high-voltage power semiconductors as facility / rack-power context, not owners of E7 generation, E2 compute silicon, or E6 systems.

docs.text: Oklo is an advanced-fission project developer focused on future power delivery. In this wiki it represents whether future microreactors and advanced nuclear projects can turn into faster data-center power, not present-day facility infrastructure or onsite electrical equipment.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the future-microreactor / contract-execution branch of spine 7, Power Generation, Grid, and Fuel Supply
  • Boundary: this page only covers generation projects, power contracts, and time-to-power realization
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local raw packet proves that the company has disclosed data-center/campus strategic relationships, power-availability partnerships, and business updates.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches realization only if those relationships turn into executed contracts, verifiable project progress, regulatory advancement, and realized revenue.
  • Current conclusion: the local evidence proves forward contract/cooperation direction, not realized data-center revenue or stable operating output.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Issuer / strategic relationship: data-center-linked cooperation material
  • Issuer / power-availability partnership: material on accelerating power availability
  • Issuer / business update: business and financial update material
  • Conclusion: this is a Needs-source future-generation benchmark; the local packet does not yet move framework cooperation into execution proof

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials emphasize its advanced-nuclear platform, long-term power relationships, and positioning around faster data-center power availability.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep OKLO as spine-7 future microreactor / contract-execution context, but not enough to write it as a realized data-center power beneficiary.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Whether framework relationships have become verifiable executed contracts and project delivery
  • Whether data-center power arrangements already map to realized revenue or stable operating results
  • Whether financing, licensing, and build timing are sufficient to support realistic time-to-power

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later local evidence still stops at partnership headlines without execution results, OKLO remains Needs-source context
  • If stronger local issuer/filing evidence shows the data-center power path lacks practical executability for too long, it can leave high-priority maintenance

docs.title: ONTO — Onto Innovation
docs.text: Last updated: 2026-07-13 CEST

docs.title: Current role
docs.text:
• Structural status: core
  • Current role: Market-found
  • Primary lane: spine 5 process-control / metrology node
  • Boundary: owns the inspection and metrology role in HBM / 2.5D / advanced packaging; does not treat ONTO as a generic semiconductor-equipment proxy
  • Action pointer: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: Business and lane position
docs.text: Onto defines itself in the issuer raw as a process-control leader spanning 3D metrology, macro defect inspection, factory analytics, and advanced semiconductor packaging. For spine 5, its key ownership is not broad semiconductor capex but the process-control / metrology node inside HBM, fan-out, and 2.5D advanced packaging.

docs.title: AI to revenue
docs.text: The AI transmission has reached order / VPA and qualification evidence. In fiscal 2025, revenue was $1.0053 billion, and the company disclosed a new Dragonfly volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027. It later disclosed Dragonfly G5 qualification for 2.5D AI packaging. The cleaner framing is that AI / HBM / advanced packaging have entered product orders and platform validation, while the local raw still does not provide a company-wide AI revenue ratio.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Fiscal 2025 revenue reached $1.0053 billion, and fourth-quarter revenue was $267 million.
  • The company disclosed a new volume purchase agreement worth more than $240 million with a leading HBM manufacturer for Dragonfly 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology supporting expansion through 2027.
  • Dragonfly G5 was qualified for 2.5D AI packaging.
  • The company defines itself as an advanced-packaging-related process-control supplier spanning wafer and package inspection / metrology.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Management said global AI investment is driving a strong upcycle in semiconductor capital-equipment spending.
  • Initial Dragonfly G5 shipments are expected to begin in June 2026, and Dragonfly platform revenue is expected to grow more than 50% in 2026 versus 2025.
  • The preliminary first-quarter revenue figure and second-quarter guidance remain management outlook rather than realized results.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: • Rising HBM, chiplet, fan-out, and 2.5D / 3D packaging complexity should increase package-level inspection and metrology content and sensitivity requirements.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Company-wide AI revenue share.

docs.title: Company kill criteria
docs.text:
• HBM / 2.5D qualifications fail to convert into sustained shipments and revenue.
  • Dragonfly demand stops broadening across customers and process layers.
  • The advanced-packaging process-control story gets fully overwhelmed by a broader wafer-equipment cycle.

docs.title: ORCL — Oracle
docs.text: Role: spine 1 demand / capacity economics Structural status: core Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-03-10; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Oracle earns subscription and usage revenue from databases, enterprise applications, and OCI. Its AI-chain role is not making chips, power, or facility equipment; it converts long-duration cloud contracts into capacity that must be delivered. The central test is whether RPO becomes capacity, revenue, margin, and cash on schedule.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: Oracle is a demand anchor in Cloud and Compute Demand. It buys GPU, network, storage, land, power, and facility delivery for enterprise and AI customers. Unlike suppliers such as NVDA, VRT, or BE, Oracle operates the capacity; its capex alone does not prove any supplier's revenue attribution.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: OCI, database, and application contracts first enter RPO. Revenue is recognized as Oracle delivers capacity and services. AI raises compute usage and campus intensity, but value capture depends on delivery speed, contract mix, pricing, financing cost, and post-capex cash conversion.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q3 FY2026 RPO was USD 553B, up 325% year over year.
  • Cloud Infrastructure / IaaS revenue was USD 4.9B, up 84%; total cloud revenue was USD 8.9B.
  • It disclosed USD 30B of bond and mandatory-convertible-preferred financing, making the capital-structure constraint explicit.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • Oracle maintained FY2026 capex guidance of USD 50B and raised FY2027 revenue guidance to USD 90B; both remain undelivered forward guidance.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: Contracted demand at this scale should support power, facility, interconnect, cooling, and storage procurement. Supplier share, timing, and margin still require company-specific order evidence.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text: RPO is not all AI, near-term, or high-margin revenue. Capex does not automatically improve FCF or identify a particular equipment beneficiary.

docs.title: Value capture and misread boundary
docs.text: Oracle's advantage is its database/application installed base, multicloud connections, and large OCI contracts. The market already sees the demand; the open question is RPO conversion, capacity delivery, and financed returns.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• RPO grows while IaaS revenue conversion keeps slowing.
  • Capex and financing rise without improvement in operating margin, FCF, or leverage.
  • Power, GPU, network, or construction delays block contracted capacity.
  • Large contracts are renegotiated, cancelled, or carry poor pricing/mix.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: ORCL is a Core / Market-found demand entity and capex-spillover validator. Any current action lives only in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: PDD — PDD Holdings
docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme portfolio prose; China ecommerce and Temu platform owner Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence as of: 2026-07-13; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: PDD's stable position is a China ecommerce and Temu cross-border commerce platform. Recommendation, advertising, and algorithmic capabilities matter, but this is first a commerce-platform owner, not an AI-revenue owner and not a finance, application-software, or infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PDD sits on the platform-tech / internet side of E10 cross-theme portfolio prose. Its stable ownership is the China ecommerce and Temu platform. It does not absorb the finance-owner roles of UPST, PGY, or KLAR, and it does not turn recommendation, advertising, or merchant tooling into an independent application or infrastructure owner.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: PDD's AI relevance mainly comes from recommendation, advertising distribution, search ranking, and merchant / consumer matching efficiency, but those technologies are a secondary mechanism rather than the page's primary ownership. FY2025 reported revenue and profit prove commerce scale, but broad commerce totals are not AI revenue. Merchant, advertising, or transaction totals do not automatically equal AI proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The local source manifest and FY2025 SEC 6-K provide issuer / SEC-level evidence for the ecommerce and platform business.
  • The PDD and Temu business frame can be written durably as a China ecommerce / cross-border commerce platform rather than a peripheral sample.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• The local SEC / issuer evidence supports value capture through the merchant, consumer, and transaction-fulfillment network.
  • That framing proves commerce-platform positioning, but it does not by itself prove recommendation or advertising technology as separated AI revenue.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If the platform keeps improving matching efficiency, user retention, and merchant productivity, technology investment should keep serving commerce economics.
  • That technology value belongs first to ecommerce-platform execution, not to an independent AI-software owner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local source set does not isolate AI revenue.
  • Broad GMV, revenue, advertising, or merchant totals are not automatic proof of AI monetization.

docs.title: Value capture and boundary of misread
docs.text: PDD captures value by turning traffic distribution, transaction matching, fulfillment, and cross-border platform capability into a scaled commerce engine. The misread boundary is treating broad commerce totals as AI revenue, or expanding recommendation / advertising technology into an independent application or infrastructure owner. PDD owns the ecommerce / Temu platform role here, not a finance or AI-infrastructure role.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If commerce growth, merchant economics, or cross-border fulfillment pressure deteriorates, platform value capture gets hit first.
  • If regulation, cross-border policy, or platform-governance issues weaken Temu or PDD transaction efficiency, the E10 ownership should contract.
  • If later local issuer / SEC evidence still cannot separate technology capability from independent AI monetization, this page should keep refusing to rewrite broad commerce totals as AI revenue.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: PDD is Active / Market-found. Its stable ownership is the China ecommerce and Temu platform. Recommendation and advertising technology stay secondary mechanisms and cannot absorb finance, application, or infrastructure owner boundaries. Any current action lives only in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: PDFS — PDF Solutions
docs.text: Role: spine 5 manufacturing / packaging / test / materials active; yield / process-control analytics data layer Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence through: 2026-07-02; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: PDF Solutions mainly sells the analytics, connectivity, and process-control software layer for fab + assembly + test. Its AI relevance comes from the data-management and yield-improvement complexity of advanced packaging and test, not from any physical-equipment node.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PDFS primary-owns the yield / process-control analytics data layer inside Semiconductor Manufacturing, Advanced Packaging, Test, and Materials. It is not a bonder, substrate supplier, inspection tool, or OSAT-capacity owner; it provides the software, connectivity, and analysis layer that stitches together fab, assembly, test, and backend equipment data.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: As advanced packaging and test become more complex, data standardization, yield analysis, and process control become more valuable. PDFS's current revenue bridge comes from Exensio usage in Intel AP&T and OSAT settings, CIM300 backend connectivity, and a business scale already visible in Q1 2026 revenue, margins, and backlog.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 quarterly total revenues were $60.1m, up 26% YoY; GAAP gross margin was 72%, non-GAAP gross margin was 76%; GAAP operating margin was 10%, non-GAAP operating margin was 25%; ending backlog was $246.4m.
  • The Intel page is explicitly titled Leveraging PDF Exensio for Intel Advanced Packaging and Test and says advanced packaging / testing creates major data-standardization and analysis challenges; Intel uses Exensio to manage and analyze manufacturing data from wafer fabrication to final testing.
  • Exensio OSAT is explicitly for Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test companies and includes process control, test operations, and assembly operations.
  • Exensio platform text says it spans fabrication, testing, assembly, and enterprise processes and states 55,000+ fab tools connected, 40,000+ process tools under process control, and customers across 350 organizations / 20 countries.
  • CIM300 explicitly says GEM300 standards can be adopted on semiconductor backend equipment, including packaging assembly and test equipment, even when the substrate is not a wafer.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: • The Intel use case, OSAT positioning, and platform-scale metrics all come from issuer / product-page language; they prove product presence and routing but not a separate advanced-packaging / test revenue split by themselves.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: PDFS is a beneficiary of advanced packaging / test yield and process-control analytics, but the page only stays clean if it keeps the “data layer, not physical equipment” boundary explicit. It currently looks former-half-hidden: no longer totally overlooked, but also not one of the most crowded first-line hardware bottlenecks.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• AP&T / OSAT revenue mix is not separately disclosed.
  • Intel revenue contribution, customer concentration, and the share of backlog tied specifically to packaging / test are not disclosed.
  • It is not proven that PDFS should be written as a hardware bottleneck owner inside advanced packaging.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• Intel / OSAT use cases remain showcase references instead of scaling commercially.
  • Platform breadth and connected-tool scale stop translating into backlog, margins, or retention quality.
  • The market starts treating PDFS as an equipment play and the thesis boundary becomes distorted.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: PDFS is an Active / Market-found yield / process-control analytics name with a former-half-hidden workflow modifier. The key requirement is to preserve the boundary that this is an analytics data-layer name, not a physical-equipment name.

docs.title: PGY — Pagaya Technologies
docs.text: Role: E10 cross-theme portfolio prose; B2B credit-decisioning and securitization infrastructure owner Structural status: active Formal discovery state: Market-found Evidence as of: 2026-07-13; action SOT: Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Pagaya's stable position is machine-learning-driven credit-decisioning, matching, and securitization infrastructure for banks, lenders, and funding partners. The boundary to defend here is B2B credit infrastructure, not a consumer entry point, merchant network, or broader ecommerce / application platform.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: PGY sits on the fintech / consumer-credit side of E10 cross-theme portfolio prose. Its stable ownership is B2B credit-decisioning and securitization infrastructure. It does not absorb UPST's AI/ML lending marketplace, KLAR's BNPL / digital-bank / merchant-consumer network, or PDD's commerce / application-owner role.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: Pagaya's AI relevance comes from embedding machine learning into credit decisioning, funding routing, and securitization execution, not from broad funding or credit totals. This page only treats AI relevance as revenue-relevant when issuer / SEC evidence keeps tying those model capabilities to platform fees, partner take rates, decision efficiency, or asset performance. Funding, credit, or merchant volume does not automatically equal AI proof.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Local issuer source defines Pagaya as an AI-driven consumer-credit platform serving partners.
  • The FY2025 results page provides issuer-primary annual business evidence supporting the view that its core role is B2B credit decisioning and securitization execution infrastructure.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Issuer framing consistently emphasizes machine learning, an AI-driven approach, and partner enablement.
  • That framing proves platform positioning, but it does not by itself prove AI as a separately monetized revenue line.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If partner adoption and funding capacity hold, Pagaya's matching, structuring, and securitization platform can amplify operating leverage.
  • That leverage belongs to B2B credit-infrastructure execution, not to consumer-app, BNPL-network, or commerce-traffic ownership.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local source set does not isolate AI revenue.
  • Broad funding, asset-performance, or total matching scale is not automatic proof of AI monetization.

docs.title: Value capture and boundary of misread
docs.text: Pagaya captures value by turning credit decisioning, funding distribution, and securitization workflow into reusable platform capability for partners. The misread boundary is turning it into a consumer-facing lender, merchant network, or generic commerce / application owner. PGY owns B2B credit-decisioning / securitization infrastructure here; it is not a substitute for other finance or commerce owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If partner concentration or funding appetite contracts, platform volume and securitization elasticity get pressured together.
  • If model performance or regulatory scrutiny weakens partner trust, the AI framing falls back toward a normal structured-credit operator.
  • If later local issuer / SEC evidence falls back to broad funding or asset totals without more specific decisioning, take-rate, or execution proof, this page should narrow its AI-relevance language.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: PGY is Active / Market-found. Its stable ownership is B2B credit-decisioning and securitization infrastructure. It does not absorb the owner boundaries of UPST, KLAR, or PDD. Any current action lives only in Tech Mainline Research Unified Ticker Ledger.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Palantir turns deployed compute into enterprise and government operational deployment software revenue. The key issue is not how fast broad PLTR growth looks in one quarter, but whether those deployments keep compounding into repeatable commercial and government software revenue rather than just sustaining very high expectations.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: E9 AI Application Production and Data Lifecycle enterprise / government AI software deployment owner, focused on landing models and compute into real operating, decision, and execution layers.
  • Boundary: it does not own E2 compute silicon, E6 systems manufacturing/integration, or any E7/E8 power and facility layer.
  • Distinction: PLTR is not CRM's customer-data suite and not NOW's workflow-ticket owner. It is closer to deployment programs, operational stack, and enterprise / government software landing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• As enterprise and government customers expand software deployment across more use cases, users, and tasks, Palantir can convert that into larger platform contracts and revenue.
  • The acceleration in U.S. commercial and broader U.S. revenue shows that this path is real, but broad company growth is still not the same as standalone AI revenue.
  • The real test is deployment breadth, repeatability, and cross-customer replication, not treating all revenue as one single AI product bucket.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Q1 2026 revenue growth was +85% year over year.
  • U.S. revenue growth was +104% year over year.
  • U.S. commercial revenue growth was +133% year over year.
  • Rule of 40 score was 145%.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to about +71% growth.
  • The local source spine classifies PLTR as a software-platform name with hard AI evidence, not just concept narrative.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• PLTR sits at the operational landing layer after compute is already deployed, so enterprise and government rollout can continue absorbing platform spend once infrastructure is in place.
  • That makes it an E9 software-deployment owner rather than an infrastructure owner.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not split out a standalone AI product-bucket revenue bridge or a finer commercial versus government AI revenue bridge.
  • Broad company growth, U.S. growth, and commercial growth are not all directly attributable AI revenue.
  • The current local packet also does not prove that this growth has already become broader, more diversified long-duration revenue quality.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If very high growth starts depending on a small set of large programs and cross-customer repeatability weakens, the E9 owner case should be downgraded.

  • If deployment quality weakens on either the commercial or government side, the broad AI software deployment thesis needs to be rewritten.

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Plug Power sells fuel-cell systems, hydrogen supply, and related infrastructure capabilities. In this wiki it is not an ordinary data-center onsite-power company; it is a special case for whether hydrogen-product relevance can convert into data-center revenue before capital-structure stress overwhelms the path.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text:
• Lane: the hydrogen-optionality branch of spine 7, Onsite Bridge Power, Storage, and Backup
  • Boundary: this page only covers generation products, fuel supply, and time-to-power realization constraints
  • It does not own site switchgear, rack power, cooling, EPC/MEP, or any spine-8 infrastructure delivery in Facility Electrical, Rack Power, Cooling, and Delivery

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text:
• Realized results: the local filing and product materials show that the company explicitly treats data-center power as an application path and has a corresponding high-power fuel-cell platform.
  • Forward path: the AI/data-center narrative reaches realization only if issuer disclosure converts that application path into named projects, repeat orders, verifiable revenue/backlog, and sustainable unit economics.
  • Current conclusion: the existing filing does not break data-center activity into auditable commercial results, and capital-structure pressure remains the dominant constraint.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• Filing / issuer-primary: the Q1 2026 Form 10-Q and FY2025 annual filing define the current disclosure boundary.
  • Product / commercial materials: the GenSure HP launch and electricity-rights monetization materials show the product path and asset actions behind the hydrogen-power narrative.
  • Conclusion: the evidence currently reaches application direction and product preparedness, not data-center commercial revenue with healthy economics.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text: Company materials identify data-center power as a target application and present platform and asset actions intended to support that path.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text: That is enough to keep PLUG in the hydrogen / capital-structure special-situation bucket, but not enough to restore it to the ordinary onsite-power ranking.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• Named data-center projects with realized revenue or backlog
  • Repeat-deployment economics, gross profit, or operating performance
  • A sustainable business path that no longer depends on recurring financing support

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later issuer evidence still stops at application language without data-center commercial realization, PLUG remains context-only and does not re-enter the ordinary ranking
  • If capital-structure or operating stress overwhelms product optionality to the point that the path is no longer realistically executable, it can leave ongoing spine-7 maintenance

docs.title: In plain language
docs.text: Powell owns medium-voltage switchgear and in-site power distribution within E8, taking power that has already reached the site and routing, protecting, and distributing it to critical loads inside the campus.

docs.title: Lane and boundary
docs.text: POWL's primary lane is medium-voltage switchgear, site power distribution, power control rooms, e-houses, and integrated power packages. It is the owner of in-campus power distribution and control equipment; it does not own utility interconnection or substation EPC, it does not own rack-side UPS or thermal infrastructure, and it does not own upstream generation and fuel assets or server and networking-system manufacturing.

docs.title: How AI becomes revenue
docs.text: After external power reaches an AI campus, it still has to be safely distributed to buildings, modules, and critical loads. Powell monetizes the layer where power is on site but not yet reliably distributed across the campus through switchgear, distribution systems, PCR and e-house products, and integrated power packages.

docs.title: Proven
docs.text:
• The Q1 FY2026 results raw file explicitly discloses data-center orders well in excess of USD 100M, including a megaproject booking of about USD 75M, proving the company has won real datacenter electrical-delivery demand.
  • The Integrated Package Solutions product page shows Powell is not just selling a single cabinet; it also offers power control rooms, e-houses, and more integrated in-site distribution solutions.

docs.title: Issuer claim
docs.text:
• Company framing presents datacenter orders, integrated package solutions, and more complex electrical-delivery requirements as growth drivers.
  • The current local issuer and product evidence supports Powell's effort to expand through higher-spec electrical packaging, but that remains issuer framing rather than a disclosed long-duration AI revenue structure.

docs.title: Reasonable inference
docs.text:
• If AI campuses keep scaling in size and load density, the content per project for in-site medium-voltage distribution, protection, and modular electrical rooms should rise, making Powell's revenue bridge broader than standalone switchgear.
  • POWL is distinctive because it sits after the utility handoff and before rack and facility thermal infrastructure, owning the middle layer where in-site distribution actually has to get built.

docs.title: Not proven
docs.text:
• The current local evidence does not show a durable revenue and margin conversion path from datacenter orders, and it does not prove that this order intensity will persist.
  • The current local evidence does not support Powell owning utility interconnection or substation EPC, or rack-side power and thermal infrastructure; those remain separate owners.

docs.title: Risks and kill criteria
docs.text:
• If later disclosure shows datacenter orders are not converting into sustained in-site distribution revenue, or integrated packages are not increasing content per project, the E8 owner thesis weakens.
  • If execution remains too project-custom and value capture stays thin, Powell's stability inside E8 declines.
  • If the page starts extending Powell into utility-interconnection ownership, upstream generation and fuel ownership, or rack-thermal ownership without local-source support, that is a kill signal.

docs.title: Current role
docs.text: Role: Core / Market-found; modifier: former-half-hidden. Stable E8 owner for medium-voltage switchgear and site power distribution; not an E7 generation/fuel owner and not an E6 server or networking-system manufacturer.
